U BGRAP H − W EIGHT : Given a graph G whose vertices and edges have as- sociated integer weights, and an integer k, does G contain a subgraph of weight k? (Define the weight of a graph to be the sum of the weights of the vertices and edges of that graph.)  prove this is NP-Complete

message.content:
To start our proof we need basic definitions.
First let us clearly define what is meant by NP membership here.
The problem belongs to nondeterministic polynomial time because verification is straightforward.
We can verify a proposed subgraph in polynomial time by summing weights correctly.
Now we must show that this specific problem is actually hard enough.
We will reduce the Subset Sum Problem to this Weighted Subgraph Problem instance.
Subset Sum is known to be NP-complete so this reduction works perfectly well.
Given integers $a_1, \dots, a_n$ and target $K$ we construct graph $G$ carefully now.
Create one vertex $v_i$ for each integer $a_i$ with weight exactly equal to $a_i$.
Add no edges between any vertices in this newly constructed simple isolated graph structure.
Set the target subgraph weight parameter $k$ equal to the subset sum target value $K$.
If there exists a subset of integers summing to $K$ then corresponding vertices form valid solution.
Conversely if a subgraph has total weight $K$ then its vertex weights sum exactly to $K$ indeed.
This establishes a polynomial time many-one reduction from Subset Sum to our specific graph problem case.
Since Subset Sum is NP-complete and our problem is in NP it follows immediately that this problem is NP-Complete too.
